sessions.title: FOMC Day Market Analysis (Wispr Flow recording)
sessions.summary: New York session on the FOMC-minutes day (release 14:00 ET; he says '11:00' on his Pacific clock). Choppy pre-news action, reduced lot size announced up front. US30 printed the only 5m double break down early; he waited for a Spotlight bearish confirmation or a proper retracement. US500 (weaker pair) then printed a 5m DB; he took a NAS sell anyway at reduced size, rolled on the first closure, and was wicked out at break-even. Later a US30 short off a 30s FVG and closure: rolled at the red dotted line (past the implied dealing range), told the room to take 50% and reduce to a 10% flyer before the Spotlight bearish confirmation printed; the confirmation printed and a retracement followed. His own broker was frozen so he could not take profit himself. Post-mortem: the NAS sell should not have been taken because a fresh DB means a 70-80% retracement into the range and the stronger pair retraces deeper. He also reviewed the prior day's Asia US30 trade (stop hunts on the 30s): an immediate rebalance is the entry and its line can never be moved; either demand a closure over the same old 30s line or take a new 30s FVG off the new leg (tap + close); his error was using the rebalance's entry without its FVG. Order block rule: when the DB leg is a single candle with no FVG, the candle's midpoint stands in for the 5m FVG step. Advised staying out of the PM session.

events.setup: US30 is the only index with a 5m double break to the downside; no 5m FVG yet
reasons: need either a bearish confirmation from Spotlight or a proper reversal setup / retracement into a 5m FVG
FOMC minutes day: erratic price action before the release
events.quote: US 30 is the only one that's given us a double break to the downside, so I'd need to see either a bearish confirmation from Spotlight or a proper reversal setup. Retracement. Five-minute fair value gap.

events.setup: Red-folder news day (FOMC minutes): reduced lot size or stay out; check the economic calendar every morning
reasons: erratic price action before the release
volatility rises approaching the release
events.quote: On a day like this, while we have FOMC meeting minutes at 11:00, always proceed with caution. Or stay out completely. So anything that we do would be a reduced lot size. ... Forex Factory. Economic calendar. You got to check it every morning.

events.setup: M signal with no 5m FVG behind it
reasons: no 5m fair value gap = false M model
no room (wedged under the DB reversal area / 4H)
events.quote: We don't have a 5-minute fair value gap either, so it is a false M model. This would be the perfect place to drop it. ... I need a fair value gap. Even if it's a 30-second fair value gap, I need something from this.

events.setup: NAS sell at reduced lot size right after US500 (the weaker pair) printed a fresh 5m double break; US30 still had no 5m FVG
reasons: liked the room to the downside
would have to roll as soon as price reached the 1m gap / 4H
confluences: 4H FVG below as target area for US500
events.result_detail: Rolled the stop on the first closure; price climbed back, he considered moving the stop up to stay safe, then was wicked out at break-even. Post-mortem: should not have entered - a fresh DB means a 70-80% retracement into the range and the stronger pair retraces deeper.
events.quote: Reduced lot size. Looking at Nas for a potential setup, but I'd have to roll as soon as we hit this. ... I'll take Nas for a sell. ... Oh, it just wicked me out. Out. ... Once that double break happened, we knew a retracement was coming, and obviously the stronger pair was going to retrace deeper. ... It's not a question of securing yourself. Shouldn't have entered.

events.setup: US30 left and tapped a 1m FVG; looking for a short but the 30s candle closed back inside at the last second
reasons: no closure over the series yet
one more chance only, otherwise back to NAS
events.quote: Looking at US 30 for a potential setup short here. ... oh wait, no, sorry, just close back in. Literally at the last second. That's one that we had to wait. ... I'm only going to give this one chance.

events.setup: US30 sell: 30s FVG printed, closure over the series; roll at the red dotted line (past the implied dealing range); target the 4H below
reasons: 30s FVG and a big closure
US30 telling the most consistent story
roll as soon as price crosses the DR edge
events.result_detail: Rolled the stop at the red dotted line; told the room to take 50% and reduce to a 10% flyer before the Spotlight bearish confirmation printed; the confirmation printed and a retracement followed; price reached the 4H. His own broker was frozen so he could not take profit himself.
events.quote: I'll do US 30 sell. I got to roll here, though. ... That's when we are past the implied dealing range. ... Feel free to take 50 off the table. Secure yourself. ... reduce your position down to 10%. Let the 10% ride, because there could be a retracement coming. ... That's the spotlight confirmation. That could cause a retracement. I would leave a 10 flyer and/or just close off your position here.

events.setup: A fresh 5m double break = 70-80% chance of a retracement back into the range; never enter against it
reasons: the stronger pair retraces deeper before the drop
events.quote: The second a double break happens. 70 to 80% chance you're going to get a retracement back into the range.

events.setup: Order block: when the DB leg is a single candle with no FVG, measure that candle and use its midpoint as the 5m FVG step; build the 1m/30s logic off it
reasons: there was no fair value gap in the double break leg
he counts only the candle, not the 3-candle area
events.quote: I took that candle's entire measurement to see if we came back into the midpoint. And then built logic off of that 1 minute 30 seconds. So I used that as a 5-minute fair value gap.

events.setup: Review of the prior day's Asia US30 trade (repeated 30s stop hunts): an immediate rebalance is the entry and that line cannot be moved; after a sweep either demand a closure over the same old 30s line or take a NEW 30s FVG off the new leg (tap + close). His error: used the rebalance's entry without its FVG
reasons: closure over a series of candles is the entry
if you change the fair value gap you get a new entry; if you keep it, the entry and tap do not change
events.result_detail: Following the logic would have given the drop at either of two later closures.
events.quote: If you get an immediate rebalance, you can't move that. ... From now on, if you get a sweep, you can't move your entry. But you can change your fair value gap. ... I used the immediate rebalance without using its fair value gap. I used its entry. ... Entry should have been closure under here if I was still using this fair value gap.

events.setup: Journal every trade win or loss; stay out of the PM session on the FOMC-minutes day; new members watch all videos before trading in the room
reasons: volatility rises into the release
memory recall is as important as pattern recognition
events.quote: I'd stay away from the PM session today, guys. ... Probably shouldn't have even traded the New York session, but I saw a decent pattern setup. ... Always go back to every single trade, win or lose. Make sure you're journaling it.
